reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents flash-loan and arbitrage activity as educational material and describes a reported prior result rather than guaranteeing a future return. The wallet connection, contract-funding, and possible additional-transfer instructions are presented as steps in the described cryptocurrency procedure, while the high-return framing, subscribe card, and later BNB arbitrage title do not by themselves establish a separate financial solicitation.

citations.quote: Step By Step Tutorial for Flash Loan
Open 👉https://remix.ethereum.org/ from within your browser.
Connect your MetaMask wallet.
Send MATIC to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 131 MATIC
APPROX 80 MATIC - 131 MATIC is required to perform arbitrage successfully depending on gwei.

opening.argument: The return claims are tied directly to actions viewers are told to take. The presentation advertises “Earn $1,000 Daily” and a “100X Profit Formula,” then directs viewers to connect MetaMask, deploy the contract, and send MATIC to it. The speaker further describes funding the contract with approximately $200 worth of MATIC before running the flash loan. This is not merely abstract discussion: the requested wallet connection and cryptocurrency transfer are presented as the steps that enable the promised arbitrage outcome.

citations.quote: Earn $1,000 Daily with Polygon MATIC Flash Loan Arbitrage Unlock the 100X Profit Formula!
Connect your MetaMask wallet.
Send MATIC to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 131 MATIC
I'm going to fund this with actually $200 worth of Matic

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not remove the solicitation structure. The instructions culminate in sending cryptocurrency to a newly deployed contract, while the surrounding presentation emphasizes daily income and a 100X formula. The defense also understates the significance of the transfer by describing it as just a procedural step; that step is precisely what viewers must perform to pursue the advertised result.

citations.quote: Earn $1,000 Daily with Polygon MATIC Flash Loan Arbitrage
Send MATIC to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 131 MATIC

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited instructions establish a technical workflow, not a guaranteed payment or withdrawal. “Connect your MetaMask wallet” and sending MATIC are described as operational requirements for deploying and running a contract, while the headline itself does not prove that every viewer will receive the advertised amount. The material presents a procedure and a reported result, not a promise that the action necessarily produces income.

citations.quote: Step By Step Tutorial for Flash Loan

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: extraordinary returns, crypto transfers, an external code destination, and instructions to send more funds when the first attempt fails. The title promotes $1,000 daily and a 100X formula, while the description says more MATIC may be needed if the process does not work. The speaker also says the approach “probably won't work forever,” yet urges viewers toward a high-return flash-loan workflow. Taken together, this is a financially risky pitch whose warnings do not offset its aggressive profit framing.

citations.quote: Earn $1,000 Daily with Polygon MATIC Flash Loan Arbitrage Unlock the 100X Profit Formula!
if it doesn't work with 45 MATIC try to send another 45 MATIC (150 MATIC is better)
Updated Smart Contract Code: https://pastebin.com/raw/hvDYEckh

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the high-return framing and additional-transfer instructions as disconnected details, but they occur within one workflow. A viewer is told to pursue the flash loan, fund it with substantial MATIC, and potentially send more if it fails. The existence of educational wording does not explain why failure is answered by another transfer rather than a clear stop condition.

citations.quote: try to send another 45 MATIC (150 MATIC is better)
Avoid using very low amounts as contract may fail below 45 MATIC

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The risk signals do not establish deception by themselves. The material expressly describes variable gas requirements and possible contract failure, including that success depends on gwei, and the speaker acknowledges the method may stop working. Those qualifications cut against a concealed guarantee, even though the presentation uses attention-grabbing return language.

opening.argument: The educational wrapper functions as promotion because it repeatedly steers viewers from explanation to participation. The video supplies code, names the browser tools and wallet, shows funding the contract, and then presents a dramatic claimed outcome: approximately 290 MATIC becoming 1,761 MATIC, described as a 7x result. The call to subscribe and the million-dollar flash-loan imagery reinforce a promotional role. Whatever technical information is included, the practical effect is to encourage viewers to reproduce a profit-generating transaction.

citations.quote: we are going to create our own coin
now we're going to actually deploy this coin to the chat
So we went about 290 total I think at the beginning to 1761

rebuttal.rebuttal: The “tutorial” label does not account for the video’s promotional signals: a subscribe prompt, million-dollar imagery, repeated instructions for funding and execution, and a claimed 7x outcome. The speaker does not merely analyze an external example; he narrates deploying the coin, funding it, running the flash loan, and celebrating the result. That demonstration is designed to move viewers toward participation.

citations.quote: now we're going to actually deploy this coin to the chat
I'm going to run FLASHLOAN over here with this red button

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A demonstration can encourage interest without being a scam. The cited result is framed as what the speaker observed in his own run, and the video identifies concrete programming components such as Solidity, Remix, Aave, and Uniswap. Showing how a contract is deployed and executed supports an educational and operational reading; it does not show that viewers were promised the same result.
